qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Vertically integrated farm-to-fork processing offers cost efficiencies, but selling fresh pork and poultry predominantly as private label to a concentrated UK grocery oligopsony leaves Cranswick with thin 6.5-7.5% operating margins and no independent consumer pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Over 75% of revenue is concentrated in major UK supermarkets (Tesco, Sainsbury's, Marks & Spencer). While highly efficient and vertically integrated, Cranswick produces predominantly private-label fresh protein with thin ~7% operating margins and lacks independent pricing power against concentrated buyers.
qualitative.evidence: Customer concentration is extreme with over 75% of sales to UK supermarket giants. Operating margins remain thin at 6.5%-7.6%, reflecting structural buyer power. While ROCE is healthy at 16-18% due to disciplined plant investments, GAAP ROIC hovers around 11.5%-13.1%, and the business lacks independent consumer brand pricing power or switching costs to pass through structural agricultural cost surges without supermarket pushback.
